newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP says hard to overcome copper falls.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP says hard to overcome copper falls.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) managing director John Prescott said on Friday that overcoming the low copper price in the coming quarters would be a difficult task if prices did not improve.
He said he would not give any numerical profit forecasts for the coming quarters and through the financial year.

"Clearly unless there's some changes in copper prices which I'm not prepared to predict we have a big task again in overcomign the impact of lower copper prices," Prescott told a news conference. BHP earlier reported a 23 percent fall in net profit to A$287 million for its first quarter to August 31.
However, Prescott said the effect of lower copper prices would not be so great in the current quarter ended November 30.
"That impact might not be as great quarter on quarter as it was in the August quarter, because the November figure was somewhat lower than the August figure of last year," he said.
"Also, the steel market will be a challenge quarter on quarter," he said.
Net profit before minorities from BHP's copper division was A$85 million for the August quarter, 55 percent down on the same quarter a year earlier because of lower prices.
BHP estimated the effect of the lower copper prices had adversely impacted profit by A$150 million.
The steel division's contribution to the quarterly results was a net profit before abnormals of A$90 million, 38 percent below the corresponding period a year earlier.
Prescott said he saw the group making progress in flat steel production and also in its petroleum division.
"We will continue to see reasonable shipments from minerals across the current product range--in iron ore, manganese and coal," Prescott said.
BHP shares closed five cents lower at A$16.04 on turnover of 4.01 million shares.
